item.title: Sánchez and Lula meet in Madrid to strengthen ties amid 'threat of the far right'
item.description: The two leaders are said to have discussed their "bilateral agenda" and reaffirmed their intention to continue strengthening cooperation between Spain and Brazil.

item.title: Europe Tonight: MEPs debate Rwanda deportation scheme announced by five EU countries
item.description: On Euronews' first edition of Europe Tonight, presenter Mared Gwyn Jones led a debate on Europe's latest migration crackdown, after five EU countries announced a partnership with Rwanda to establish deportation hubs for irregular migrants.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV struck in eye by rosary during tour of South America
item.description: The pontiff was able to continue with his schedule and appeared to be uninjured. Leo's tour of South America has also seen him visit Uruguay and Argentina and came just weeks after he underwent lung cancer surgery in Rome.

item.title: Video shows rocket failure that destroys 40 Amazon satellites
item.description: A United Launch Alliance Vulcan rocket suffered an in-flight failure minutes after liftoff from Florida, leaving 40 Amazon internet satellites unable to reach orbit.

item.title: France can no longer support Kyiv 'financially,' Le Pen tells Ukrainian ambassador
item.description: The National Rally party's stance on Ukraine has come under increasing scrutiny over its pledges to withdraw financial aid and questions over historical ties to Russia.

item.title: Germany's 'bratwurst tax' sparks backlash as community groups face new VAT rules
item.description: Under new rules, public bodies such as municipalities and towns are to be generally liable for VAT when they engage in commercial activities.

item.title: Qatar Sustainability Week explores ways to cut food waste, track carbon emissions and support wellbeing
item.description: Wasting less and looking after our physical and mental health were among the themes of this year’s Qatar Sustainability Week. Schools, businesses and communities explored how the choices we make when shopping, eating and going about our day can affect both the environment and our wellbeing.

item.title: Italian schools hit by new wave of bomb and poison threats
item.description: Under new security guidelines, Italian schools are no longer automatically evacuated in response to vague, mass-distributed threats, with the decision left to the discretion of law enforcement and security officials.

item.title: Euronews Verify: Is Europe prepared and able to defend against hybrid threats?
item.description: Amid disinformation, cyberattacks and bomb hoaxes, hostile countries and groups are testing Europe's vulnerabilities. Is Europe prepared, or even able, to defend itself?

item.title: Europe Tonight: Five EU states announce Rwanda deportation hubs as EU warns Russia is ‘weaponising winter’
item.description: Five EU nations announce Rwanda deportation hubs by mid-2027. Plus, EU aid chief Hadja Lahbib warns Russia is weaponising winter in Ukraine, Lithuania’s FM Kęstutis Budrys opposes Moscow talks before a ceasefire, and Robert Pattinson is revealed as the next James Bond.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 16th, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 16th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: French football chief Diallo set to run against Infantino for FIFA presidency
item.description: The next FIFA presidential election is due to take place at the 77th FIFA Congress on Thursday, 18 March 2027 in Rabat, Morocco.

item.title: Serbia to accelerate work on EU accession, Student List representative says
item.description: Serbia’s Student List will speed up rule-of-law reforms needed for EU accession, MP Aleksandar Baucal said in the movement’s first international appearance.

item.title: All the ladies in the house: RAYE and Rosalía lead the way for 2027 Grammy nominations
item.description: Europe's leading songstresses are frontrunners for top awards at the 2027 Grammys. With 11 nominations, British singer RAYE has equalled Beyoncé's 2025 record number of nods while the American star has now become the most-nominated Grammy artist in history with 100 nods.

item.title: Prince William and Princess Catherine play street cricket with locals in Mumbai
item.description: Prince William and Princess Catherine play street cricket with local players in Mumbai, India, during a three-day visit for the Earthshot Prize.

item.title: Trump says he could meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un in China
item.description: Trump is planning to discuss nuclear disarmament when he meets with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China this week.

item.title: Five EU countries unveil Rwanda deportation plan in migration crackdown
item.description: Denmark, Austria, Germany, the Netherlands and Greece aim to begin deporting rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda in 2027, despite concerns over human rights and potential legal challenges.

item.title: Countries to decide future of 'killer robots' at UN conference
item.description: UN Secretary General and Pope Leo XIV have urged countries to agree stricter rules for autonomous weapon systems, to stop them from being given the ability to make life and death decisions without human intervention.

item.title: Meet the new James Bond: It's Pattinson, Robert Pattinson
item.description: Daniel Craig’s successor has been confirmed after a long casting process, making Pattinson the seventh actor to play the role of 007.

item.title: ECB warns AI share boom could end in 'abrupt repricing'
item.description: Eurozone funds have bought heavily into the technology, leaving European savers exposed if the boom turns to bust in the US.

item.title: President Trump says he 'wouldn't mind' Jensen Huang being reinstated as Nvidia CEO
item.description: The comments come as a petition calls on Nvidia to reinstate Huang.

item.title: 12 crew members rescued after cargo ship capsizes off Bulgaria following suspected drone strike
item.description: All 12 crew members working on board the vessel were rescued and were being flown by helicopter to Bulgaria's Chaika air base, according to authorities.

item.title: US clamps down on chip 'loophole' in foreign access to advanced AI chips
item.description: A new US Commerce Department rule targets foreign remote access to chips like Nvidia's Blackwell.

item.title: Revolut's Italian unit put under judicial administration after anti-money laundering failures
item.description: The measure against the digital bank was requested by the Milan Public Prosecutor's Office as part of a Guardia di Finanza investigation. According to investigators, shortcomings in control systems facilitated the concealment and transfer of €76.5 million.

item.title: Moulin Rouge dancers kick off Paris Christmas celebrations
item.description: Moulin Rouge dancers and Republican Guard musicians launch Christmas lights in Paris, France, with a French cancan performance near the Madeleine church.

item.title: Can we trust AI to guide climate policy? New report warns against glaring ‘design flaw’
item.description: AI models answer about 90 per cent of climate questions accurately in English, but quickly give in to pushback, according to a report showcased at COP31.

item.title: Belgian king grants PM De Wever more time to agree new budget
item.description: King Philippe had refused De Wever's resignation earlier this month and asked him to continue with budget talks, giving him until 16 November to solve the impasse.

item.title: Repsol sues Spanish power firms for €120m over 2025 blackout
item.description: The oil company has taken the electricity distributors of Iberdrola, Endesa and Naturgy, as well as grid operator Red Eléctrica, to court over damage to five industrial sites after the blackout that hit Spain and Portugal on 28 April 2025.

item.title: Shareholders sue Intel after its shares plunge nearly 29%
item.description: Shareholders have sued Intel after its shares fell nearly 29% in their biggest one-day drop in decades. A weaker-than-expected sales forecast exposed the impact of a deepening PC slump and Intel’s difficulty meeting demand for server chips.

item.title: Europe must embrace AI's 'creative destruction', Nobel economist says
item.description: Nobel Prize-winning economist Philippe Aghion urged the EU to encourage new players in the AI market, ease restrictions on state aid and strengthen protections for workers facing technological disruption.

item.title: Albania's Rama slams Serbian nationalist song at EU conference
item.description: Albania's PM Rama criticised a band for playing a Serbian nationalist song claiming Kosovo as Serbian land at the European Commission’s enlargement conference. Marta Kos said it does not reflect the Commission’s position, while Pristina called it unacceptable.

item.title: Move over Michelin: ‘Gold Key’ hospitality design awards crown best hotels for 2026
item.description: La Réserve Firenze, Six Senses London and 1 Hotel Copenhagen were among the European hotels recognised.

item.title: The US has lost measles-free status. What does that mean and what’s next?
item.description: In countries where measles is endemic, the virus spreads in a continuous chain from person to person for a year or more.

item.title: US airports slowly return to normal after three days of disruption caused by take-off ban
item.description: Throughout the weekend, stranded passengers wandered through chaotic airports and sat on floors, waiting for updates or to be rebooked.

item.title: Five things you need to know before Anthropic goes public
item.description: The maker of Claude wants investors to value it at more than $1 trillion (€909 billion), despite paper losses in the tens of billions and a set-up that leaves shareholders with little say.

item.title: US and Iran slide closer to fresh all-out war as new exchange of fire increases
item.description: A sudden rise in Iranian attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz follows an increasing number of air strikes between the US and Iran, as both sides trade intensifying warning shots, bringing the region closer to a new all-out war. Meanwhile, a third US aircraft carrier has arrived in the region.

item.title: Sweden calls for new EU plan to unlock frozen Russian assets for Ukraine
item.description: Sweden urged the EU to use frozen Russian assets to supprt Ukraine, with Foreign Minister Maria Malmer Stenergard telling Euronews that the financial risks should be shared among member states.

item.title: EU ministers demand united response as Russian attacks spill beyond Ukraine
item.description: Romania, Estonia and Sweden have called for a united European response to mounting Russian threats, from drone attacks in the Black Sea to suspected sabotage, as the EU weighs its role in future Ukraine peace talks.

item.title: Millions of red crabs begin annual migration on Australia’s Christmas Island
item.description: Millions of red crabs have begun their annual journey from Christmas Island’s forests to the coast, crossing roads and specially built bridges to reach the sea and breed.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 16th, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 16th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: French actor Gerard Depardieu drops appeal for sexual assault conviction
item.description: Depardieu, who has acted in more than 200 films and television series, is the highest-profile figure caught up in France's response to the #MeToo movement.

item.title: EU clears UniCredit takeover of Germany's Commerzbank
item.description: The EU has approved UniCredit’s takeover of Germany’s Commerzbank, a cross-border deal aimed at strengthening Europe’s banking sector.

item.title: Fewer students are traveling from abroad to study at US universities, new report shows
item.description: US campuses saw a 9% decrease in international enrolment this autumn compared to last year, according to a survey from the Institute of International Education.

item.title: Italy fines Meta €805m for accessing Facebook Android photos and videos without consent
item.description: The social media company has 60 days to disable the ‘Get tips from your gallery while browsing Facebook’ feature and introduce explicit consent.

item.title: 'Temu Harry Potter': New clip of HBO's series gets panned online
item.description: A new clip of the upcoming Harry Potter TV reboot has been released, and the internet is unanimous. "As a millennial who spent hours upon hours reading Harry Potter growing up, I’m insulted by this."

item.title: Carney says US tariffs could push Canadian carmakers towards China
item.description: Mark Carney has warned that US tariffs could push Canadian carmakers towards China, as Ottawa weighs alternatives to an increasingly strained North American auto market.

item.title: Take That and 'You Can See Everything': The best things to do, hear, see or watch in Europe this week
item.description: An exhibition exploring the history of drugs, the return of boy band Take That, and this year's most anticipated documentary — here's what to look out for this week.

item.title: Exclusive: EU countries weigh shorter probation period for newcomers
item.description: The Irish EU presidency proposes cutting the probation period for newcomers from 15 to 10 years, extendable by five. Member states remain split on suspending voting rights, how to trigger measures and pre-accession monitoring, ahead of a key discussion at EU ambassadors' level.

item.title: Japan’s economy stalls as inflation weighs on growth
item.description: Japan’s economy stalled in the third quarter as Iran war-fuelled inflation, bad weather and an earthquake weighed on growth. Analysts still expect the Bank of Japan to raise interest rates again in December.

item.title: Prince Harry says 'you're going to win' on surprise weekend visit to Ukraine
item.description: The British royal took to the stage at a conference for medics organised by Superhumans, a clinic in the city that specialises in the rehabilitation of wounded soldiers.
